messages:
sara: Thanks for the infra update earlier. Posting a few quick operational Qs so product/support teams can prepare comms.

michael: Are we expecting any temporary SKU substitutions during APAC/HW shipping? Customers asked if A100 vs H100 differences will change latency.

simon: Good Q. Short: SKU substitution only if we hit supply constraints. Substituted SKUs will be made available as compatible model variants (quantized or lower-seq-length profiles). We'll annotate the model catalog with expected latency deltas and a compatibility score.

tara: Will substitution be opt-in per-customer? Some enterprise customers need to opt-out to avoid subtle output/regression differences.

simon: Yes 9 enterprise customers can opt-out of substitutions in Dedicated and Private via policy flags. Hosted customers will get substitution as default for availability, with a per-org toggle coming later.

josh: On autoscale: what's the target warmup time we should expect for H100-backed pools? We need this for SLA docs.

olga: Typical warmup in our tests: 30-50s to reach steady-state for medium chat models with pre-warm=2. For cold-starts without warm pools it can be 3-4 minutes. We'll publish per-model warmup curves soon.

michael: If a region is temporarily capacity constrained, will traffic be automatically routed to multi-tenant pools in another region or to the customer's Dedicated in a different region? How do we present that to the customer?

simon: We have a routing precedence: 1) in-region compatible variant, 2) in-org Dedicated in-region spare capacity (if allowed), 3) cross-region routing to nearest region with capacity, 4) queued async fallback for non-realtime jobs. Console will show a "region fallback" banner and the routing reason; we'll also emit an audit event.

tara: Will cross-region routing be instantaneous or queued while infra spins up? We saw spikes in prior rollouts.

simon: Fast path when spare capacity exists. If we need to spin up new instances, there's a 30-90s ramp depending on pool size and model. That's why warm pools + pre-warm are recommended for latency-critical routes.

josh: For product: can we get a single-line blurb about expected user-facing latency impact when cross-region fallback happens so Support can triage?

olga: Blurb suggestion: "If your requests are routed to another region, expect an additional network RTT (typically 40-150ms) plus potential cold-starts if the target pool wasn't warm. Console will show fallback details." Feel free to shorten.

sara: Can infra confirm whether the Console will expose historical capacity shortfall graphs per-region? We'd like to add that to the incident runbook.

simon: Yes 9 Console will get per-region capacity trend charts (30/90/365 day) and a 'shortfall' overlay showing times when demand exceeded reserved capacity. We'll release the first view behind a feature flag next sprint.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: infra-routing-v2 deployed to staging at 2026-04-18T09:22Z :white_check_mark:

sara: Thanks all. If anyone needs more granular numbers for customer comms (e.g., expected warmup seconds per model class), ping me and we'll pull the bench CSV. Closing when we post the FAQ. :thumbsup:
